title: iOS 27.2 will help users move data and settings from an old app to its replacement
snippet: Starting with iOS 27.2, developers will be able to offer users a way to move their data and settings from an existing app to its designated replacement. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Starting with iOS 27.2, developers will be able to offer users a way to move their data and settings from an existing app to its designated replacement. Here are the details.

iOS to make app replacement easier

While uncommon, developers occasionally retire an existing app and launch a new one in its place, requiring users to move over to a separate app.

Even though most developers try to make that transition as seamless as possible, migrating can still require some work from the user, particularly when it involves data that isn’t stored in the cloud.

With iOS 27.2, Apple will address this with a new system-managed migration flow that can move an app’s data and supported settings to its designated replacement before deleting the old app.

Based on existing code in iOS 27.2 beta 1, users will be presented with an alert that says:

The developer recommends moving your existing “%1$@” app data and settings to the new “%2$@” app.

iPhone can do this for you now, before you start using your new app. Afterwards, the old app will be deleted from this iPhone.

Users will then be able to choose either “Move App Data and Settings” or “Don’t Move Anything.” If the user rejects the migration, iOS will present a second confirmation warning that some preferences, including notification and location settings, may need to be configured again.

To be clear, the feature appears to be limited to cases where a developer replaces one of its own apps with a designated successor, rather than migrating data between apps from different developers.

Based on the current implementation, iOS can migrate a range of system-level settings and permissions, including:

Privacy, location, and Health authorization decisions

Notification settings, including accessory notification settings

Per-app Do Not Disturb and Focus settings

App locking and protection settings

CarPlay icon order and compatible widget layouts

Live Activities and accessory Live Activities

Access to associated accessories

LaunchServices preferences, fonts, capture-related defaults, telephony data, and Secure Element services

We will keep an eye out for changes to this framework during the iOS 27.2 beta cycle and report back if we learn more about how developers will be able to implement it.

title: Here are 100+ things Siri AI can do on your iPhone
snippet: iOS 27 launched this week with the all-new Siri AI. David Pogue put the new Siri to the test by trying 125 requests, here’s how it went. more…
fullText:
iOS 27 launched this week with the all-new Siri AI. David Pogue put the new Siri to the test by trying 125 requests, here’s how it went.

iOS 27’s new Siri AI impresses David Pogue following 125 tests

Siri has been baked into the iPhone for nearly 15 years. But during that time, many Apple users have grown accustomed to only depending on Siri for certain supported tasks.

For example, I’ve long relied on Siri to create reminders, start timers, play Apple Music, and when driving I’ll use it to send messages. Outside of those few limited tasks though, Siri’s shortcomings have trained me to not rely on it.

But iOS 27’s new Siri AI is a huge upgrade that can do so much more than ever before. It might just take some time to adjust to it being your go-to, though.

That’s why I found David Pogue’s new Substack post so helpful. Titled “125 Tests of the New AI Siri,” Pogue lists out over 100 prompts he’s tried with Siri AI and details how the assistant did.

Here are a few examples that stood out to me:

28. What are people waiting on me for? (Generates list from Mail, Messages, and Reminders. Incredible. Everything I did for this column was supposed to be for testing purposes only, but this one actually found stuff I’d forgotten I was supposed to do!) […]

30. (Running late to a party:) What’s the apartment number!? (“The apartment number for the Bynum party tonight is 10-F.” Note: I never said what party or what day!) […]

46. Delete all my alarms. (“Do you want to delete 38 alarms in Clock?” Tap to confirm.)

With almost every one of the 125 tests, Siri succeeded. And among the few failures, such as sending a Venmo payment, Siri AI will likely perform better after third parties update their apps for iOS 27 and Siri AI compatibility. 

You can read the full list of 125 Siri AI examples here on Pogue’s Substack.

title: iOS 27.2 introduces Apple Health app overhaul, here’s what’s new
snippet: Today Apple released iOS 27.2 beta 1, skipping over 27.1 entirely in the testing cycle. And among other changes, the new iOS 27.2 update includes the previously announced all-new Health app. more…
fullText:
Today Apple released iOS 27.2 beta 1, skipping over 27.1 entirely in the testing cycle. And among other changes, the new iOS 27.2 update includes the previously announced all-new Health app.

All-new Apple Health app debuts in iOS 27.2 beta 1

Last week during its September event, Apple unveiled an all-new Health app that would be coming to iPhone later this year.

Now today, beta testers have received the first access to the Health app redesign via iOS 27.2 beta 1.

When Apple introduced the new Health app, it emphasized how Apple Intelligence would be used to help users better understand their health. Here’s what the company said:

The Health app has been redesigned to dynamically respond to a user’s data using Apple Intelligence, with a new Insights tab that surfaces timely health information and a new Longevity tab that analyzes a user’s longitudinal health data for deeper insights. The Longevity tab includes Health Age, an Apple Watch feature that shows users how certain metrics are tracking relative to their actual age. The Health app also includes movement evaluations that measure flexibility, strength, balance, and more using vision-based AI models on iPhone and heart rate data from Apple Watch.

Now today with iOS 27.2 beta 1, the new Insights tab and Longevity tab are both available for testing if you’re a developer.

Because the new Health app relies on Apple Intelligence, you’ll need an AI-compatible iPhone to try it out. Certain features require a paired Apple Watch too. And your device must be set to US English.

So if your iPhone is less powerful than an iPhone 15 Pro, or you don’t have a compatible Apple Watch, the Health app upgrades will be missing. But for everyone else, iOS 27.2 provides a first glimpse at Apple’s expanded vision for the Health app.

Note: Apple says additional Health features will roll out in future betas, like the ability to order labs from Quest and personalized recommendations. Also, despite its availability in the beta, Apple says the new Health app won’t actually ship in iOS 27.2 but instead is coming later in the year.

title: iPhone 18 Pro Max still uses a Qualcomm modem in the US, teardown confirms
snippet: TechInsights has published one of the first in-depth iPhone 18 Pro Max teardowns. Most notably, the teardown confirms that the iPhone 18 Pro Max sold in the United States still uses a Qualcomm modem. more…
fullText:
TechInsights has published one of the first in-depth iPhone 18 Pro Max teardowns. Most notably, the teardown confirms that the iPhone 18 Pro Max sold in the United States still uses a Qualcomm modem.

On its tech specs website, Apple says the iPhone 18 Pro uses the Apple C2 cellular modem. In every country other than the United States, Apple says the iPhone 18 Pro Max also uses its C2 cellular modem.

The company, however, doesn’t specify which modem the U.S. variant of the iPhone 18 Pro Max uses. Speculation suggested the iPhone 18 Pro Max used a Qualcomm modem, and this teardown confirms it.

According to the TechInsights teardown, the iPhone 18 Pro Max variant sold in the United States uses the Qualcomm Snapdragon X80 modem. This is the same modem used worldwide in the iPhone 17 Pro and iPhone 17 Pro Max.

So, to recap, here’s how Apple’s transition to its own in-house modem technology has played out in the United States specifically:

iPhone 16 / 16 Plus / 16 Pro / 16 Pro Max: Qualcomm Snapdragon X71

iPhone 16e: Apple C1

iPhone 17 / 17 Pro / 17 Pro Max: Qualcomm X80

iPhone Air: Apple C1X

iPhone 17e: Apple C1X

iPhone 18 Pro: Apple C2

iPhone 18 Pro Max: Qualcomm X80

iPhone Duo: Apple C2

Apple touts that the C2 brings “AI-powered improvements to cellular quality and reliability.” In comparison to the C1X, Apple says the C2 delivers “meaningfully faster uploads when compared to C1X while consuming 15 percent less energy.” The C2 modem also supports mmWave 5G, unlike the C1 and C1X.

It seems clear to me that Apple has caught up to Qualcomm, now that the C2 supports mmWave 5G connectivity. Apple’s C-series modems have always been more power-efficient than Qualcomm’s (which, I’d wager, is something most people care more about than raw download and upload speeds).

Apple hasn’t said why the iPhone 18 Pro Max still uses a Qualcomm modem. The likely explanation, though, is that the decision is purely contractual, and Apple will ditch Qualcomm once and for all as soon as it can.

title: Apple planning to sell AI servers powered by M8 Ultra chips, says report
snippet: Apple is working on plans to make enterprise servers powered by M8 Ultra chips, according to a new report. The report specifically says that the company plans to offer the AI-focused servers for sale, not just use them internally. Two versions are said to be in development, with Apple considering incorporating Nvidia networking tech in the machines … more…
fullText:
Apple is working on plans to make enterprise servers powered by M8 Ultra chips, according to a new report. The report specifically says that the company plans to offer the AI-focused servers for sale, not just use them internally.

Two versions are said to be in development, with Apple considering incorporating Nvidia networking tech in the machines … 

The Information reports that plans have not yet been finalized and that the servers are not expected to go on sale until 2029.

Apple has been developing the server with plans to sell it to AI developers, other businesses and governments, the people said. The product under consideration would come in two versions—a smaller one with two of Apple’s planned M8 Ultra chips clustered together, and a bigger one with four M8 Ultra chips.

Apple has considered connecting the M8 chips in the server using an Nvidia set of products called NVLink Fusion, which includes switches, chiplets and software that help chips communicate with each other in data centers.

Apple is said to have been working on the project for around a year, with CEO John Ternus in favor.

9to5Mac’s Take

While 2029 is some way off, and the report acknowledges that the project could be canceled before then, it does make a great deal of sense. People are already using clusters of Mac Studios to run AI models locally, so it seems clear there would be a market for more powerful Apple servers. The only question is whether this is a big enough priority for Apple to say yes to launching it.

title: iOS 27.2 lets developers use an alternative App Tracking Transparency prompt in the EU
snippet: Starting with iOS 27.2, developers will have the option to use an alternative App Tracking Transparency system prompt in the EU, as part of Apple’s recent deal with the bloc. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Starting with iOS 27.2, developers will have the option to use an alternative App Tracking Transparency system prompt in the EU, as part of Apple’s recent deal with the bloc. Here are the details.

New prompt is mandatory in select European countries

A few weeks ago, Apple confirmed it would comply with “fairer” App Tracking Transparency rules in the EU, following an investigation by Germany’s Federal Cartel Office.

The deal concluded a years-long antitrust probe into whether Apple’s ATT rules unfairly disadvantaged third-party apps compared with its own services. Apple has always denied the allegations, claiming that it applies the same strict privacy principles to its own apps from the ground up. German regulators, however, remained unconvinced.

As a result, Apple agreed to eight changes in the ATT framework in Europe, and you can read more about that here.

That said, Apple confirmed today that iOS 27 will let developers choose whether they want to “use an alternative version of the App Tracking Transparency system prompt in the EU,” and added that “due to legal requirements, only the alternative version of the system prompt is available for apps distributed in Germany, France, Italy, Poland, and Romania.”

In an update to the “User privacy and data use” developer support page, Apple elaborates on the alternative version of this system prompt:

The alternative version of the App Tracking Transparency system prompt has modified formatting and language and provides you the option to use a text button labeled “Additional Information.” This allows you to surface additional information about your request to link user or device data collected from your app with user or device data collected from other companies’ apps, websites, or offline properties for targeted advertising or advertising measurement purposes, or to share user or device data with a data broker.

The company adds that EU developers will also be able to re-prompt users one year after their previous ATT choice, regardless of whether they initially accepted or declined tracking.

title: macOS 27.2 beta 1 now available to developers, here’s what’s new
snippet: Now that macOS 27 Golden Gate is officially out, Apple is moving on to its next beta cycle, straight to macOS 27.2 beta 1. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Now that macOS 27 Golden Gate is officially out, Apple is moving on to its next beta cycle, straight to macOS 27.2 beta 1. Here are the details.

macOS 27.2 beta 1 now available

After releasing macOS 27 Golden Gate earlier this week, Apple is now rolling out the first developer beta of macOS 27.2, skipping over the 27.1 betas.

As for what to expect from this release, during its “Surprise and Shine” event earlier this month, Apple said that the new Siri AI, which launched in English, would expand to five more languages in October, including French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish. This means developers might find these languages in this first beta.

Additionally, Apple has yet to confirm a new rollout date for two features it announced during WWDC but didn’t make it to the first macOS 27 release: an agentic feature in Passwords that will automatically change leaked passwords, and suggestions in Messages conversations.

We are digging through the code to check whether these made it to macOS 27.2 beta 1 and will report back with what we find.

title: Philips Hue Bridge Pro is now $139, with even bigger price hikes globally
snippet: The Philips Hue Bridge Pro is a massive functional upgrade for your smart home lighting, but it now comes at a much higher cost, with price hikes now in effect around the globe. more…
fullText:
The Philips Hue Bridge Pro is a massive functional upgrade for your smart home lighting, but it now comes at a much higher cost, with price hikes now in effect around the globe.

In the US, Philips Hue launched its Bridge Pro last year at $99. Now, that price has jumped up to $139 across the Hue Shop, Amazon, and other retailers. It’s a price hike of roughly 40% and appears to have kicked in around mid-late August.

That’s almost certainly due to the rising costs of memory, as Bridge Pro has 8GB of RAM.

But the price hikes are even worse in other regions. Hue Blog reports that the price has jumped from an initial cost of €89 to €149 now. And that price hike appears to have just kicked in throughout Europe, with some retailers not yet showing the updated pricing. The report also notes that European prices on several other Hue products have gone up by around €10-20 each, including the Hue Essential bulb 4-pack going from €59 to €69.

title: Corridor raises $25M seed to build a health benefits brokerage for SMBs
snippet: Corridor focuses on SMBs, which it says traditional brokerages often overlook because small accounts generate lower commissions than larger accounts.
fullText:
It’s been a while since Jackson Wagner left his job as a product lead at Scale AI in July 2022. Now, he’s building in a new space altogether: The new effort is an AI health benefits brokerage called Corridor that focuses on small businesses, which it says traditional brokerages often overlook because small accounts generate lower commissions even though they take the same amount of time as larger accounts. 

Corridor is betting an AI solution may help on that front. On its platform, customers work with human advisors while AI agents do administrative tasks in the background. The company says its agents can handle tedious office work like checking whether a doctor is in a customer’s insurance network, scheduling care, or providing a doctor updated health insurance information. 

“We are every single employee and management’s concierge for all things healthcare,” Nikhil Aggarwal, the company’s CEO, told TechCrunch. 

On Monday, Corridor said it had raised a $25 million seed round led by Bain Capital Ventures. 

Corridor came about after Wagner was in a running accident, and the poor handling of his care led him down a path of “significant, consistent, chronic pain.”

“I developed a long list of complications that needed to be worked through one by one,” he said. 

He eventually left Scale AI to get a master’s degree in computer science and electrical engineering at UC Berkeley, before joining Build Robotics in 2023. Later, he teamed up with former Scale AI colleague Eric Qian to work on Capernaum AI, a startup building a clinical agent targeting musculoskeletal care and chronic pain. 

The two eventually approached Cold Start to see if they would fund Capernaum, but Aggarwal, who was a partner at Cold Start along with Jason Dong, saw a much larger opportunity. So the four of them took off and launched Corridor together. 

“Since health plans are the window through which the vast majority of Americans access health care, it became overwhelmingly clear that one of the highest impact things I could do to improve outcomes for individuals was to create a way for them to access better health plans,” Wagner said.

Other companies in this space include Ignition Benefits and Nava Benefits. 

Investors in Corridor’s round include BoxGroup, as well as executives from OpenAI, Scale AI and Ramp. The startup is now preparing for Q4, since “80% of small businesses choose their health plan in Q4,” Aggarwal said.  

“Our vision is to build the most trusted healthcare institution in America,” he said. “To earn that, we are laser-focused on a simple promise: doing what we say we’re going to do for the businesses and employees we serve.”

title: I Tried Two Extraordinary Security Gadgets Made for Spots Other Tech Can’t Reach
snippet: Home security is going in all-new directions this year. I tested Abode’s sensors for gates, garages and more in my home.
fullText:
Abode's new sensors are a winning combo. / Tyler Lacoma/CNET Art		

	

		

									

						Abode Security Sensors 2026					

					

	8.0

	
					

			

	

		

			

				Pros & Cons			

			

			

							

					
						Accurate and speedy sensors for areas other security sensors aren't made for					
				

							

					
						Tests showed excellent performance on garage door and fence gate					
				

							

					
						Abode's hub automatically connects to sensors and makes setup one of the easiest I've done					
				

							

					
						Offers a variety of automations and alert options through Abode's intuitive app					
				

							

					
						Sensors have many additional applications for sheds, tilting windows and more					
				

					

			

							

					
						Abode's standard hub requires a permanet Ethernet connection					
				

							

					
						The outdoor contact sensor design could use another pass					
				

					

	

		

A new crop of security sensors has hit the shelves in 2026, and I like what I’ve tested. Tiny sensors that can detect tampering, tilting, movement and so on are offering all-new ways to watch over specific parts of our home. Abode is the first security kit company I’ve seen embrace this tech by offering its first entirely new sensors in years, made for parts of the home that security systems don’t usually watch.

Abode has two new products available now, a sensor made to monitor garage door access ($35), and an outdoor access sensor ($50) designed for gates, sheds, barns and any door open to the elements. I got to try them both around my home, and found them particularly effective and easy to set up compared to many of the sensors I’ve tested.

If you’ve been looking for a special device to help monitor access to backyards, detached buildings on your property, or garage doors that always seem to get left open, these sensors are a remarkable answer, particularly if you already have an Abode system. If not, I’ll cover what you need to know from my testing.

Unboxing and setup

Abode’s new sensors work flawlessly with its existing hub.Tyler Lacoma/CNET

I was able to fully test an Abode starter security kit as well as its two new sensors for this review, providing a clear look at how the security brand functions. As far as setup experiences go, this has been one of my speediest. And I’ve tested many different systems.

Abode’s beginner’s kit is small, offering an indoor sensor, motion sensor and fob, along with the hub. I was pleased to find out, after downloading the app and connecting the hub, the other base devices automatically added themselves and made the setup process effortless, smoother than nearly any other security system except possibly Ikea’s affordable sensors.

Adding the new garage and outdoor sensors also proved quick, with pairing happening only seconds after I installed the batteries and typed in the activation code.

Abode’s hub connects to new sensors in a snap.Tyler Lacoma/CNET

The one problem I have with Abode’s system is how the standard hub connects to Wi-Fi. This hub requires an Ethernet connection to your router or gateway, not only during setup but all the time. That’s a not-so-small problem if, like me, you have a router, gateway and other necessary devices already taking up all nearby outlets, which forced me to jury-rig a solution for the hub while I was testing.

Abode’s Iota hub does offer Wi-Fi, but that requires a more expensive upgrade to a $200 starter kit, not including extra sensors. It’s baffling that Abode’s standard hub still doesn’t support Wi-Fi when every other brand does. Check the outlets near your router before you choose this solution.

Garage sensor installation and performance

Abode’s garage sensor can sense any kind of tilt up and down.Tyler Lacoma/CNET

Equipped with internal gyroscope technology, Abode’s garage door sensor is made to detect orientation, and setup couldn’t be simpler. Using the included adhesive strips, I slapped the small monitor on my closed garage door, and it began accurately detecting open/closed states immediately in the Abode app.

Smart garage door motors and controllers can also do something like this, plus app controls, but this is one of the first standard home security systems to expand to the garage, and adding a single $50 sensor is far more affordable than replacing your garage controller entirely. Abode let me know if the garage was left open, and advised me on unexpected garage door movement when no one was at home, just as advertised.

Placing the sensor shouldn’t be any trouble, no matter what kind of garage you have. It sticks onto the inside of the garage door where there is plenty of space, and doesn’t require any complicated calibration. You may have to reset the sensor after placement to make sure it’s reading open and closed states correctly, but that, too, takes only moments.

Finally, you could use this sensor on anything that tilts up and down like a garage door, such as tilting windows, so it could have other applications in your home.

Gate sensor installation and performance

Abode’s outdoor sensor is a little annoying to put together, but works like a charm.Tyler Lacoma/CNET

Abode’s outdoor access sensor proved more complicated than the garage monitor. Bulkier than most access sensors and equipped with weather-resistance capabilities, it’s made to tell when anything outdoors opens and shuts. The two parts sense when they are close or when they’ve moved apart, with a bit of extra leeway compared to indoor sensors, since outdoor fences and other access zones have varied designs and gaps.

The complex housing proved adequate, but was more frustrating to install and is in need of some future refinements. The screw-in backplate, for example, had pop-out sections to make room for the screws, but the plastic base was so thick I couldn’t put out the sections at all, not even with a hammer that nearly destroyed the base itself (I used another tool to carve them out eventually, not an ideal situation). And the battery casing was so tight and awkwardly designed, I was afraid forcing the batteries in would harm the nearby, unprotected circuitry.

In these ways, the design feels a little too close to a prototype model for me, and it probably needs another pass or two. But it works, and works very well, when it’s finally set up.

Connected to my old fence gate, the sensor accurately and immediately told me whenever it was opened or closed. I’ve found that gate left open more than a few times, so this gave me welcome peace of mind. I also tested it during a stormy downpour, which did nothing to affect the performance of the sensor.

You may want to turn off beeps from the hub that sound every time it alerts to the sensor being opened, but Abode provided a setting to do just that. However, alerts and monitoring aren’t the only things these sensors can do.

App automations that benefit from Abode’s support

Abode’s app allows for customizations and automations, too.Tyler Lacoma/CNET

One of the most impressive parts of Abode’s security platform is how it maintains connections to other third-party smart home gadgets, from Google Home connections to the rare-to-find Apple support for certain devices. There are also Abode’s own devices, including cameras and smart locks, which naturally work with the system

Abode’s CUE function offers automations similar to Google Home or Apple Home.Tyler Lacoma/CNET

When Abode’s system is armed, triggering one of these garage or gate sensors can trip the system and sound a siren. But using the CUE automation tool in the Abode app, I found you can also set up many other types of automations, depending on what you want to activate.

This can include setting lights to turn on a warning glow if a fence gate is left open, or automatically unlocking your door when the garage is opened. You can also set times for these triggers to work, so they only function in the evening, on weekdays or only trigger after a certain time (the gate has been left open for 2 hours, for example). This adds more possibilities if you want to expand your smart home, but it’s not necessary to get value out of these sensors.

Remember, Abode’s app can also support third-party integrations with other devices.Tyler Lacoma/CNET

If you want to pay for an Abode subscription, you can add more features with plans starting at $80 a year, but these are mostly camera-focused, and I don’t think they’re necessary for these sensors at all.

Final thoughts on Abode’s new access sensors

Abode’s sensors signal helpful new trends in the home security world.Tyler Lacoma/CNET

Abode’s newest sensors offer exceptional performance in spots other sensors aren’t really made for. They’re also more expensive than typical sensors, and the outdoor sensor might need another design pass in the future, but I otherwise found them easy to set up and start using for customized, helpful alerts.

One word of caution: Abode’s standard hub requires an Ethernet connection, so consider where you’ll put it, and if you’ll need to run Ethernet cable anywhere during installation. Otherwise, this system sets itself up in minutes.

I’m enjoying this 2026 wave of security tech innovations. They’re finding new applications in the home – and finding them with success. Aqara’s multipurpose sensor is one such model. Abode’s proved another strong example, so if you’ve been looking for extended security capabilities outdoors or in the garage, take note of this update.

		

				

					

						

													

					

					

						

Tyler Lacoma
						

						

							Senior Editor / Home Security and Smart Home						
					

											

								

											Tyler has worked on, lived with and tested all types of smart home and security technology for over a dozen years, explaining the latest features, privacy tricks, and top recommendations.
With degrees in Business Management, Literature and Technical Writing, Tyler takes every opportunity to play with the latest AI technology, push smart devices to their limits and occasionally throw cameras off his roof, all to find the best devices to trust in your life. He always checks with the renters (and pets) in his life to see what smart products can work for everyone, in every living situation. 
Living in beautiful Bend, Oregon gives Tyler plenty of opportunities to test the latest tech in every kind of weather and temperature. But when not at work, he can be found hiking the trails, trying out a new food recipe for his loved ones, keeping up on his favorite reading, or gaming with good friends.

title: iOS 27.2’s First Developer Beta Brings These Features to Some iPhones
snippet: The developer beta includes updates to apps like Facetime and Podcasts.
fullText:
Just two days after Apple released iOS 27 to the general public, the tech giant released the first developer beta for iOS 27.2. While iOS 27 brought Siri AI and more to your device, this early look at iOS 27.2 shows Siri AI expanding to other languages and a few upgrades in other apps, like Facetime.

If you’re wondering what happened to iOS 27.1, Apple has said the foldable iPhone Duo will launch on 27.1 next month, and all devices will be able to update to 27.2 sometime later.

Since this is a beta, I recommend downloading it only on something other than your primary device. This isn’t the final version of iOS 27.2, so the update might be buggy and battery life may be short — it’s best to keep those troubles on a secondary device.

Also, since this isn’t the final version, more features could end up landing on your iPhone when Apple releases iOS 27.2. 

Here are some features developers can try now in the first iOS 27.2 developer beta.

Siri AI in more languages

In iOS 27, Siri AI is only available in English. But the first developer beta of iOS 27.2 expands Siri AI to French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese and Spanish.

Apple previously said Siri AI would expand to these additional languages, so this shows the company moving quickly on that promise.

Use front and rear cameras simultaneously in Facetime

In the first developer beta of iOS 27.2, you can use your front and rear facing cameras at the same time in Facetime calls. This allows you to Facetime call with a larger group of people — you don’t have to squeeze everyone into a single frame in order to see the person on the other end of the call. However, everyone on the call needs to be on iOS 27 or later for this feature to work.

	

			

Refreshed Podcasts options

The Podcasts app also gets an update in the first iOS 27.2 developer beta. The beta introduces two rows to the top of the Home tab within the app: New Episodes and Continue Playing. This can help you keep track of what podcasts are new and what podcasts you still have to finish. 

It’s a small, pleasant addition to the interface, and I appreciate how it helps keep my podcasts organized.

Apple TV profile expansion

In the first developer beta of iOS 27.2, you can create TV Profiles in your Apple TV app. You can assign a profile to your child or someone else and ensure your preferences aren’t messed with. 

So if you’re tired of being recommended kids shows after letting your child watch the series Shape Island, you can create a profile for your child and let them watch those quirky little shapes all they want. (But also, it’s possible that I like Shape Island more than my son does, so you should check it out.)

Apple TV multiview on iOS

Another Apple TV update in the iOS 27.2 developer beta is Multiview. Developers who subscribe to Apple TV can watch up to four live sports streams, including streams from Major League Soccer and Formula 1, at once. That way, you don’t miss an important game, or you can look at a map of the racecourse while watching feeds from driver-view cameras.

Updated Health app

Developers can see a redesigned Health app in the first developer beta of iOS 27.2. However, the redesign is expected to launch sometime later this year, despite being featured in this beta.

Those are a few of the new features developers can try now with the first developer beta of iOS 27.2. There will likely be more betas before the OS is released to the public. Apple has not said when exactly it will release iOS 27.2 to the general public, but we expect it to land on devices in October.

For more, here’s what to know about iOS 27 and why your battery might be draining faster after updating. You can also check out why the iPhone Duo will launch with iOS 27.1.

title: Vocci’s ring adds a new form factor to meeting note-taking
snippet: Vocci's lightweight ring costs $249, and might pose some privacy questions.
fullText:
There is no dearth of different forms of hardware for meeting note-taking, including pendants, pins, and credit-card-styled devices. That hasn’t stopped Vocci from releasing a new device for the same use case in a ring form factor, which is convenient but could create some privacy issues.

The ring form factor is one of the easiest for anyone who wants to just press a button and have the device start recording. Pebble’s new Index 01 Ring, which I am testing right now, lets you hold the button and take a note or a reminder. Stream Ring, made by Sandbar, works similarly with a control pad on the top. Vocci’s ring takes a different path, with meeting note-taking as a central function.

The ring has a button, which you can double-tap to start recording and double-tap again to stop. You can tap and hold the button to ask Vocci AI questions, but that only works when you have the app open. There is an indicator light and a haptic motor for recording feedback. The ring is lightweight at under six grams and uses titanium material on the inner and outer surfaces — likely a coating.

The company claims that the Vocci ring can record notes for eight hours on a single charge. The device comes with a chunky plastic case, which can charge the ring up to three times.

Image Credits:Vocci

The device captures meetings very well. I have had conversations spanning more than an hour in loud cafes, and the ring managed to convert most of the chat into accurate transcripts. However, this method of note-taking is not great if you want to take short notes. 

The software is the disappointing part of the Vocci ring. The app itself is a bit confusing. Whenever I took shorter notes, I saw AI-generated insights that were longer than the notes themselves. Each recording has Chat, which is the main transcript; Highlights, which are short snippets you can capture by pressing the button while recording a conversation; and Notes, which is a summary and insight of the whole conversation. 

In the app, there is a tab called Base where you can find transcripts, recordings, and anything you generate from them, and I found that redundant. I didn’t find a way to directly initiate a chat with AI for session transcripts. 

Voice-enabled rings are a great form factor for taking short notes or reminders. The app doesn’t have direct integration with reminder apps, which is a bummer. The feature rollout for its software is also slow. The company informed me that users can use Vocci’s Model Context Protocol (MCP) to connect to other assistants, but the option to do that didn’t appear until a few weeks ago in the app. Other meeting notetakers are building their platforms to allow users to automate insights and workflow through AI, and at the moment, Vocci’s platform is not fully built out for that. 

There are some privacy concerns with this device because of its form factor. Vocci’s ring looks like a regular piece of jewelry until someone notices the button on it. The ring has a recording indicator, but it faces the user. It’s best practice to let someone know that you are recording a conversation, and it’s also required by law in some countries and regions. But with this kind of device, some miscreants can easily choose not to disclose that information and record the conversation without anyone noticing. The company said it encourages people to disclose that they are recording, but that may not be enough.

At $249, the ring is pricey compared to other note-takers like Plaud or Pocket, and that is due to the device’s lightweight form factor. The ring is for someone who doesn’t want to stick a gadget on the back of their phone, wear a wristband, or wear a pendant. On the hardware layer, a lot of these devices are combinations of some microphones, a battery, and a connection to the phone. We will likely see more variety in hardware meeting note-takers in the coming years, until users pick the specific formats that work for them.

title: SwiftKey ‘AI voice’ is Pixel 11’s Rambler voice-to-text for other Android phones, works offline
snippet: Rambler in Gboard is perhaps one of the best Pixel 11 features, delivering powerful voice-to-text backed up by AI models. Once you’ve used it, it’s hard to switch back to anything else, but the Microsoft-owned SwiftKey is testing out a new “AI voice” feature that brings the core functionality of Pixel 11’s Rambler to basically any other Android phone. more…
fullText:
Rambler in Gboard is perhaps one of the best Pixel 11 features, delivering powerful voice-to-text backed up by AI models. Once you’ve used it, it’s hard to switch back to anything else, but the Microsoft-owned SwiftKey is testing out a new “AI voice” feature that brings the core functionality of Pixel 11’s Rambler to basically any other Android phone.

Available in the latest SwiftKey for Android beta release (v9.13.16.4), “AI voice” is an enhanced voice-to-text feature that allows you to speak and then let the AI step in to clean up filler words, format text, and more. In other words, it’s Pixel 11 Rambler, just without the exclusivity.

You tap a microphone icon to get started, with no live preview showing (the one thing we don’t love about Rambler) and a checkmark button ending the session, leaving the AI to process the result. 

Android Central notes that you’ll need to download an offline language model for “AI voice” to work, which is one big difference – it works offline, no servers required. The publication says that testing the feature on a Fold 8 required only 163MB of storage and worked with the device fully offline, something you can’t do with Rambler on the Pixel 11 series. Droid-Life also tested it out, finding that you can’t use voice commands to edit the test as Rambler allows, but it gets the job done.

	

While it initially seemed like Rambler might not be a Pixel exclusive, that’s where we’re at right now, so “AI voice” in SwiftKey is probably a good alternative for many. Wispr Flow is also available, as we previously covered, though its lack of keyboard integration can be a bit annoying at times.

You can download the SwiftKey for Android beta through the Play Store.

title: iOS 27: My favorite new iPhone features (other than AI)
snippet: Apple released iOS 27 to everyone this week, and the headlining changes are Siri AI and the array of new Apple Intelligence features. However, the update also includes plenty of non-AI features. Here are a few of my favorite iOS 27 features (other than Siri and AI). more…
fullText:
Apple released iOS 27 to everyone this week, and the headlining changes are Siri AI and the array of new Apple Intelligence features. However, the update also includes plenty of non-AI features.

Here are a few of my favorite iOS 27 features (other than Siri and AI).

The new Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features are fantastic in iOS 27, but there are some others: 

In the Music app, Apple has updated AutoMix with new transitions. I was a big fan of the initial version of AutoMix that launched in iOS 26, and the new transitions in iOS 27 are noticeably better and more immersive.

In the Photos app, iCloud Shared Albums now offer full-resolution sharing. This is a big upgrade that makes it significantly easier to share photos and videos with others without compromising image quality.

You can now set an independent volume for alarms in the Clock app. This new option is in the Settings app under “Sounds & Haptics.” This means your alarms and timers no longer have to match your ringtone volume.

iOS 27 adds an all-new extra-large widget size for your Home Screen. There are full-screen widgets for apps like Music, Photos, Weather, and Calendar.

You can now swipe away the Now Playing widget from the Lock Screen in iOS 27. 

On the Lock Screen, you can now move the clock to the top widget row, so it no longer gets in the way of your wallpaper.

In the Photos app, you can now save a specific video frame as a photo. This means you no longer have to manually take a screenshot of a video you’ve already taken to get a specific frame as a separate photo.

The Apple Pay checkout flow has been significantly overhauled, making it a lot easier to switch between payment cards.

iOS 27 adds landscape support to more apps, which is great as someone who keeps their iPhone docked at their desk all day. This includes apps like Music, Reminders, Weather, and more.

The Find My app has a new design in iOS 27, plus more flexible sharing options. In particular, I like that the new design shows me more specific location information without having to tap on a specific person.

When you copy something to your iPhone’s clipboard in iOS 27, you’ll see a built-in paste shortcut above the keyboard the next text field you go to. This makes it a lot quicker to copy and paste text, links, photos, and more between apps.

In CarPlay, there’s now an audio scrubber that lets you skip to different parts of a song or podcast right on your car’s display.

title: iOS 27 makes your iPhone faster in these 30+ ways

fullText:
iOS 27 is now available to everyone, and one of the big changes is that it makes your iPhone a lot faster. In fact, Apple has outlined more than 30 ways in which your iPhone will be faster after you update.

How iOS 27 makes your iPhone faster

When Apple announced iOS 27 in June, the company emphasized that it combed through its software to make it faster and more reliable. “Improvements across platforms push key system capabilities forward so everyday tasks feel faster, smoother, and more enjoyable,” Apple said.

Here are more than 30 ways iOS 27 makes your iPhone faster:

Faster loading of new captures in Photos (up to 70% faster)

Faster to open full-screen view from Photos widget

Faster rendering of Collections tab in Photos

Faster to start uploading to iCloud Photos

Faster Camera launch in Low Power Mode

Faster to add recent camera captures in Messages

Faster start page content loading in Safari

Faster web application performance in Safari

Faster handling of JavaScript in Safari

Faster message loading in Mail

Faster HomeKit accessory pairing

Faster smart home accessory updates

Faster Now Playing view loading in Music

Faster Apple Music playback start

Faster board previews in Freeform

Faster data updates in the Health app

Faster workout start in the Workout app

Faster Lock Screen switching

Faster app launches (up to 30% faster)

Faster AirPlay connections to Apple TV and HomePod

Faster network file browsing

Faster and more reliable NFC reading

Faster Voice Control response in iOS

Faster entry and exit from Assistive Access and Guided Access modes

Faster PDF saving

Faster Text Recognition in photos and documents

Faster Rapid Return to Service

Faster loading of emoji and sticker keyboards

Faster shortcuts and actions indexing in Spotlight

Faster multilingual text processing for handwriting in multiple languages

Faster AirDrop transfers (up to 80% faster)

Faster AirDrop recipient discovery

Faster access to shared content on iCloud.com

9to5Mac’s Take

iOS 27 is compatible with iPhone models dating back to the iPhone 11. In fact, Apple even says that some of its performance metrics are based on testing it conducted with the iPhone 11 lineup.

For example, Apple says that apps launch up to 30% faster with iOS 27. This statistic is based on testing Apple performed on the iPhone 11 Pro Max, comparing app launch speeds between one model running iOS 26.4.2 and another running iOS 27.

All of this is very impressive — especially for people using “older” iPhone models. Apple has fixed enough bugs and made such a jump in performance that I think most iPhone users will notice a big improvement when they install iOS 27 later this year. It’s particularly impressive when you consider Apple made all these improvements to performance while simultaneously implementing a ground-up revamp of Siri.

title: iOS 27 adds scam-prevention feature to iPhone, here’s how to enable it
snippet: iOS 27 introduces a new security feature called ‘Impersonation Risk Detection’ that helps protect you against scams, but it’s off by default. Here’s what the feature does, and how to enable it. more…
fullText:
iOS 27 introduces a new security feature called ‘Impersonation Risk Detection’ that helps protect you against scams, but it’s off by default. Here’s what the feature does, and how to enable it.

Impersonation Risk Detection in iOS 27 can detect suspicious activity in real time to prevent scams

Every day around the world, people get tricked into sharing sensitive information like bank details or other financial info with bad actors.

This commonly happens via text messages, emails, or phone calls to iPhone or Android devices. And while iOS has built-in tools like call and message screening, those tools can’t prevent a scam if you choose to take action on it.

But iOS 27 introduces a new level of scam-prevention with a security feature called ‘Impersonation Risk Detection.’

Here’s what it does, per Apple’s website:

Impersonation Risk Detection helps protect against active social engineering scams. In these scams, an attacker might pose as a bank, government agency, or someone you trust to pressure or guide you into making a payment or changing your account details. Traditional security measures like two-factor authentication can’t always detect this kind of scam. That’s because you’re taking the action, even though you’ve been tricked or pressured.

Impersonation Risk Detection analyzes information about your device and Apple Account to help detect signs of an active scam. Based on this analysis, it returns a risk level to the app. The app receives only the risk level, not the underlying information used to generate it. The app decides what to do next. For example, it might ask you to verify your identity, add a delay, or show a warning.

You can turn Impersonation Risk Detection on in iOS 27 by going to Settings ⇾ Privacy & Security ⇾ Impersonation Risk Detection then toggling on ‘Share with App Developers.’

Impersonation Risk Detection is only available in supported apps, and Apple hasn’t published a list of those apps at the moment. But once enabled, it provides the app with a “risk level” while omitting the underlying information driving it. Risk levels include:

Unknown: No evidence of suspicious activity was detected

Medium: Some signs of suspicious activity were detected

High: Significant signs of suspicious activity were detected

Once the app has this risk level, it decides what action to take. For example, it may prompt you to offer additional authentication, or show a warning message related to scams.

For more details on how the feature works using ‘Trust Insights,’ see our coverage here.

title: Apple pushes UK court to lift secrecy around encryption backdoor order
snippet: In a hearing today, Apple challenged the UK government’s refusal to publicly confirm whether it has issued an order requiring the company to provide access to encrypted user data. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
In a hearing today, Apple challenged the UK government’s refusal to publicly confirm whether it has issued an order requiring the company to provide access to encrypted user data. Here are the details.

A bit of context

Early last year, The Washington Post reported that the British government had secretly ordered Apple to create a security backdoor into all iCloud content uploaded by users worldwide.

The order itself was also subject to strict secrecy rules, preventing even Apple from publicly confirming or discussing the demand.

The British government has maintained a policy of neither confirming nor denying the existence of individual orders of this kind, while companies subject to them are also restricted from disclosing that they have received one.

As a result of the reported but officially unconfirmed order, Apple removed the option to enable Advanced Data Protection (ADP) for iCloud users in the UK.

That’s because with ADP enabled, iCloud Backup and other additional categories of iCloud data are end-to-end encrypted. So instead of complying with the UK’s backdoor order, Apple stopped offering ADP to new users in the UK altogether, even though the original order reportedly applied to users worldwide.

At this point, Apple’s fight with the UK government was two-pronged: it was challenging both the underlying demand for access to encrypted data and the secrecy rules preventing it from publicly discussing that demand.

In April, 2025, judges rejected the UK government’s attempt to keep even the basic details of Apple’s legal challenge secret, ruling that disclosing the existence of the case would not harm national security.

A few months after that, the British government gave up on requiring data from American users as part of the secret mandate, as a result of pressure from the White House. The demand did not disappear entirely, however: Britain later issued a new notice targeting Apple users in the UK.

Fast-forward to a few weeks ago, when it emerged that Apple had launched a second legal challenge against the UK government after the original worldwide order was replaced by a new one specifically targeting British users.

Which brings us to today.

Apple challenges mandate secrecy

As reported by Reuters, Apple today challenged the UK government’s continued refusal to confirm or deny the existence of the new Technical Capability Notice during a hearing before the Investigatory Powers Tribunal (IPT) in London.

According to Reuters, Apple’s lawyer argued that the government’s secrecy policy prevents meaningful public discussion of the case, and undermines the principle of open justice.

From the report:

At Thursday’s hearing at the IPT, Ben ​Jaffey, the lawyer for campaign groups, Privacy International and Liberty, said the government’s position had “become farcical”.

“The horse has long bolted,” he noted, ‌meaning ⁠it was already public knowledge.

U.S. politicians and officials had publicly referred to the original notice while unnamed UK government sources had also confirmed it to the press, he said.

Both he and Apple’s lawyer said that the UK government’s NCND policy was an affront to open justice and prevented meaningful public discussion of the issue.

To be clear, today’s hearing focused on the secrecy surrounding the order, not on whether the UK government was legally entitled to demand access to Apple’s encrypted data in the first place.

Following today’s hearing, the IPT will now decide whether the government can continue relying on its “neither confirm nor deny” policy in this case. Reuters says a full hearing on Apple’s challenge to the underlying Technical Capability Notice is unlikely before next year.

title: The new Boox e-ink devices get Android 16 out of the box, including Palma 3
snippet: Boox just announced three new e-ink devices on Android 16; the largest tablet is available now, but you’ll have to wait a little longer for the updated Palma 3. more…
fullText:
Boox just announced three new e-ink devices on Android 16; the largest tablet is available now, but you’ll have to wait a little longer for the updated Palma 3.

E-ink devices have taken off in the last couple of years for a couple of reasons. The main reasoning that comes to mind is the natural disconnect that comes from using an e-ink device instead of a traditional modern OLED smartphone or tablet. Another likely has something to do with the universal appeal of an e-reader or note-taking device that lets you access apps from the Google Play Store.

Boox announced three new additions to its lineup of Android e-ink devices:

Boox Note Air6 C

Boox Note Mini C

Boox Palma 3

All three will run Android 16 out of the box, which is notable because the latest public version of Android is only one generation ahead of that. It wouldn’t have been a surprise if these devices were still a generation or two behind that. Two could be considered tablets, while the Palma is a generational upgrade to the company’s beloved compact e-reader that looks like an Android phone, at first glance.

	

The Note Air6 C is the only model Boox says is available starting today. It’s the workhorse of the three, with a new internal processor and a reasonable 3,700mAh battery. The new processor boosts the Note Air6 C’s performance with features like Dual Notes that let you annotate two documents in split-screen mode.

Boox mentions the large Android tablet also has new AI features for transcripts and document scanning. But the real improvement might just be an upgraded refresh rate that increases performance by up to 40%. Refresh rates have always been a sore point for e-ink tablets, but it’s always come with the territory for a paper-like display.

The 10.3-inch tablet has a color display that works with the included Pen3 stylus. It also wouldn’t be a Boox tablet without a front-light with temperature controls for any-time viewing.

The Note Mini C isn’t available to order just yet. It’s an 8.52-inch Android e-ink tablet aimed at users who need a little more portability from Boox devices. Similar to the Note Air6 C, it has a Kaleido 3 color e-ink display with a front light, as well as an octa-core processor. It has a little less battery power at 3,150mAh. On an e-ink tablet, that still goes a long way.

We’re also getting an upgraded model in the Palma series with the Palma 3. The form factor has grown more popular since Boox began teasing the Picco. The Palma 3 is slightly bigger and has a 6.13-inch display.

This version has a “refined anodized aluminum frame” instead of the plastic exterior seen on the previous models. The rear panel is made from fiberglass that has a “paper-textured” feel. Under that panel sits a 3,950mAh battery, which hasn’t changed from even the original Palma.

Boox hasn’t announced a release date for the Note Mini C or the Palma 3, but the Note Air6 C is available now. The Note Air6 C starts at $579. Boox’s Note Mini C is priced at $579, too, and the Palma 3 will be $339 at launch.

title: Samsung’s battery upgrades for Galaxy S27 Ultra and Pro leak – is it enough?
snippet: A new leak reveals the battery sizes of Samsung’s upcoming Galaxy S27 Ultra and S27 Pro including some long overdue upgrades, but do you think it’s enough? more…
fullText:
A new leak reveals the battery sizes of Samsung’s upcoming Galaxy S27 Ultra and S27 Pro including some long overdue upgrades, but do you think it’s enough?

Following Samsung’s adoption of silicon-carbon battery tech on the Galaxy Z Fold 8 series, it was inevitable that the Galaxy S27 series would jump on board. That’s not directly confirmed yet, but a regulatory leak (via GSMArena) offers a look at the rated capacities of Samsung’s new flagships.

These are rated capacities, with advertised capacity generally being a bit higher. As a comparison, the Galaxy S26 Ultra has an advertised battery capacity of 4,855 mAh, but an advertised capacity of 5,000 mAh. So, with that in mind:

Galaxy S27 Ultra: Rated 5,534 mAh | Advertised likely 5,700~ mAh 

Galaxy S27 Pro: Rated 5,087 mAh | Advertised likely 5,200~ mAh 

There’s no direct comparison for the Pro model, but the Galaxy S26 sits at 4,300 mAh at around the same physical size, so this is a huge jump. 

	

For Samsung’s full-size flagship, the Galaxy S27 Ultra is looking at a jump of around 700 mAh. It’s only 14%, but that’s a considerable step up after years of stagnation. Both devices are also listed with 60W wired charging.

But, in a world where silicon-carbon batteries are pushing Android flagships upwards of 6,000, 7,000, and even bigger batteries. The Oppo Find X10, for example, is rumored to pack in an 8,000 mAh battery when it debuts later this month. 

What do you think? Did Samsung do enough? Sound off in the comments below.

title: HomeKit Weekly: Homey’s new Device Updates feature shows what Matter was supposed to be all along
snippet: Firmware updates have been the weakest link for a decade with smart homes. Every sensor, light bulb, and smart lock in your house runs software that should be updated regularly. This is on top of even if they have software updates. Homey just announced a fix for a big piece of that, and the way it handles Matter devices is the part that Apple Home users should take note of. more…
fullText:
Firmware updates have been the weakest link for a decade with smart homes. Every sensor, light bulb, and smart lock in your house runs software that should be updated regularly. This is on top of even if they have software updates. Homey just announced a fix for a big piece of that, and the way it handles Matter devices is the part that Apple Home users should take note of.

HomeKit Weekly is a series focused on smart home accessories, automation tips and tricks, and everything to do with Apple’s smart home framework.

Device updates from one place

Homey’s new Device Updates feature lets you update Matter, Z-Wave, and Zigbee devices directly from the Homey Mobile App or Web App. You can update a Matter light, install a security patch for a Z-Wave lock, or improve a Zigbee sensor’s reliability, all without ever opening a manufacturer’s app. You start the update, and Homey handles the rest, including delivery, progress tracking, and a notification when it’s done. Updates are available in More > Settings > Device Updates or in each device’s Maintenance settings.

For Z-Wave and Zigbee gear, updates are delivered via their respective Homey apps, so availability depends on the developer and manufacturer. The launch list of supported vendors is already pretty solid: IKEA, Aeotec, INNR, Niko, Inovelli, Zooz, frient, ThirdReality, EcoDim, HeatIt, Namron, amina, CTM Lyng, and Nous have added support, with more to come soon.

“Device firmware rarely gets updated because the process is cumbersome,” said Stefan Witkamp, CEO at Athom. “By handling device updates inside Homey, we make it practical for both users and developers. That makes the whole smart home more dependable.”

The Matter part is the real story

For Matter devices, Homey doesn’t rely on manufacturer apps at all, and manufacturers don’t need to update their Homey app for it to work. Homey checks the Connectivity Standards Alliance’s Distributed Compliance Ledger for available Matter firmware updates. The DCL provides the firmware version, download URL, file size, checksum, and applicability information. Homey then retrieves the firmware from the manufacturer-provided URL and delivers it to the device using Matter’s standardized OTA update mechanism.

The DCL is basically a trusted public registry for Matter products, run by the same organization that certifies them and is behind the Matter standard itself. Manufacturers publish firmware update metadata to the Matter Distributed Compliance Ledger, allowing Homey to discover and grab the available updates.

This means that the update path for Matter devices isn’t tied to any one company’s app or cloud service. It’s part of the actual Matter standard itself, verified by the certification body, and any Matter controller could implement it.

If you don’t see an update you expect, it’s usually because the device’s Homey app doesn’t offer it yet, or the manufacturer hasn’t published one. Device Updates is available on Homey Cloud, Homey Pro (2023 through 2026), Homey Pro mini, and Homey Self-Hosted Server, and requires v13.2.0 or later of the Homey Mobile App.

Eve devices now work with Homey, thanks to Matter

Speaking of Matter doing what it promised, there’s a second piece of Homey news worth covering. With Homey Pro and Homey Pro mini acting as Matter Controllers and Thread Border Routers, Matter-enabled Eve devices now work with Homey. That covers favorites I’ve written about plenty in this column: Eve Energy, Eve Door & Window, Eve Motion, Eve Thermo, Eve Weather, Eve MotionBlinds, and more.

Eve has always been one of the most trusted and privacy-focused brands in the smart home (with deep Apple Home integration), with no cloud service, no registration, and no tracking. If you’re running Eve gear in Apple Home today, nothing changes. What’s changed is that the same Thread and Matter foundation that made Eve great in Apple Home now makes it portable across other platforms, and that flexibility is exactly the point of the Matter standard. It’s a protocol vs a platform.

Wrap up

For years, the smart home industry has promised interoperability and delivered walled gardens with extra steps. Simply working with the big 3-4 major platforms isn’t enough. This Homey news is what the long-term benefits of Matter are proving to bring: firmware updates going through the standard body itself.

Matter has taken plenty of criticism for moving slowly, but features like this are why it matters.

title: Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking powers Gemini Live, Gmail, & Keep
snippet: Google today announced Gemini 3.8 Live and Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking as its “most advanced live dialogue models yet.” more…
fullText:
Google today announced Gemini 3.8 Live and Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking as its “most advanced live dialogue models yet.”

Following the launch of 3.1 Flash Live in March, the new models aim to “make conversing with AI feel more intuitive and intelligent.” 

As the name suggests, Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking offers “increased intelligence and multi-step reasoning.” It’s meant for high-complexity tasks like the recently launched Gmail Live (conversational search), Docs Live (draft generation and editing), and Keep Live (note creation). The model is also beginning to roll out to Gemini Live today.

3.8 Live Extended Thinking “reasons and speaks simultaneously.”

	

It delivers increased intelligence for complex workflows while maintaining an uninterrupted conversational flow — using early verbal cues like “Let me check that…” to acknowledge prompts naturally, and live progress narration to walk users through multi-step background tasks as they progress.

In terms of benchmarks: 

“…the #1 overall spot on Artificial Analysis’ Speech to Speech Quality Index (82.6)”

“…leads in agentic task completion with 68.6% on τ-Voice”

“…35.1% on Sierra’s τ-Voice-banking benchmark”

“…strong reasoning capabilities, scoring 97.7% on Big Bench Audio, while maintaining a highly competitive price point compared to other frontier models.”

Meanwhile, the Gemini 3.8 Live base model offers “conversational intelligence with fluid dialogue and visual grounding.” The model can process “visual inputs in near real-time,” with tools and API calls executing in the background while the conversation continues. 

Users can expect the model to “acknowledge requests and keep chatting while tasks finish in the background.” Additionally, it can detect and transition between 97 supported languages mid-conversation. 

It’s “built for scale and cost efficiency” with a “second place in the Speech Agent Arena.” Gemini 3.8 Live will power AI Mode’s Search Live experience.

title: New California law will penalize influencers who don’t disclose political ads
snippet: The new legislation adds teeth to disclosure requirements for online influencers who are paid to post about politics.
fullText:
In Brief

Posted:

9:30 AM PDT · September 20, 2026

Image Credits:Kilito Chan / Getty Images

		

							

											
									

					

	

New legislation signed by California Governor Gavin Newsom adds teeth to disclosure requirements for online influencers who are paid to post about politics.

The New York Times reports that California already required disclosure for influencers who post about state or local races — but when someone failed to disclose, there were no fines or criminal penalties. (Texas also requires disclosure for paid political content, and other states are considering similar regulations.)

Under the new bill, AB 1130, regulators can fine influencers up to $5,000 for each violation, and they can also refer them to law enforcement for potential misdemeanors. 

According to the NYT, billionaire Tom Steyer, who unsuccessfully campaigned for the Democratic nomination for California governor earlier this year, paid dozens of influencers to post about his campaign online, and many of them did not initially disclose the payments.

Newsom signed the legislation as part of a broader package of bills that his office said will protect against potential election interference from President Donald Trump. The bill’s sponsor, Democratic Assemblyman Marc Berman, said that he introduced the bill after realizing there was “a bit of ambiguity about the [existing] law and how it’s enforced.”

title: Apple Music in iOS 27: Five new features just added for iPhone
snippet: iOS 27 brings new features to apps like Apple Wallet, Calendar, Notes, Maps, and more. Apple Music adds a variety of improvements too, including five new features outlined below. more…
fullText:
iOS 27 brings new features to apps like Apple Wallet, Calendar, Notes, Maps, and more. Apple Music adds a variety of improvements too, including five new features outlined below.

#1: Landscape mode

iOS 27 adds support for landscape layouts to many system apps, including Apple Music. The feature will be especially nice on iPhone Duo, but other iPhone models benefit too.

With landscape mode, you can view music artwork alongside playback controls just like in portrait orientation. 

More important to me though, lyrics are now available side-by-side with artwork. I’ve found this a great way to enjoy music while my iPhone is docked on a desk or kitchen charger.

#2: AutoMix improvements

AutoMix debuted last year in iOS 26, but Apple has upgraded and expanded it this year in iOS 27.

Per Apple’s press release:

AutoMix has added a whole new layer of energy and excitement to the experience with even better transitions that feel more immersive and engaging for listeners. AutoMix will also be available on Apple Music in tvOS and on HomePod.

Like my colleague Chance, I’ve definitely found AutoMix transitions improved this year. In iOS 26 I sometimes loved the feature and other times found it frustrating. In iOS 27 so far it’s been almost entirely a positive for me.

#3: New design for artist pages

Artist pages get a refreshed look in iOS 27, with a design that takes inspiration from iOS 26.4’s updates for albums and playlists.

Like albums, artist pages now have fullscreen color backgrounds that complement their header image. You can see several examples above.

Artist pages also make key controls more convenient to access, and their featured music title is more prominently displayed than before.

#4: Friends playlist

Apple’s roster of weekly-updated ‘Made for You’ playlists expands in iOS 27 with a new Friends playlist. Per Apple’s description:

The best of what your friends are listening to. Updated every Thursday.

The playlist is a convenient new way to get a taste of your friends’ current favorites. Each track shows you which friend is listening to it too.

iOS 27 introduces an extra-large widget size for the first time, and Apple Music takes advantage of it more than any other app.

Apple Music has three new extra-large widgets: 

Recently Played

Recommendations

Top Charts

These widgets can be added to your Home Screen or Today view, offering more flexibility in personalizing your iPhone.

title: Clicks Communicator lands in December with 12GB RAM, two months of free data
snippet: Clicks — the company bringing physical keyboards back to mobile — is getting ready to ship its first-ever Android smartphone, and it’s shaping up to be a pretty interesting device. Ahead of its launch later this year, the company is upgrading a handful of the Clicks Communicator’s specs and announcing new accessories, protection coverage options, and eSIM plans. more…
fullText:
Clicks — the company bringing physical keyboards back to mobile — is getting ready to ship its first-ever Android smartphone, and it’s shaping up to be a pretty interesting device. Ahead of its launch later this year, the company is upgrading a handful of the Clicks Communicator’s specs and announcing new accessories, protection coverage options, and eSIM plans.

When the company announced the Clicks Communicator back at CES this year, it was primarily pitched as a secondary device meant to pair with your main smartphone. It seems like the team has heard from its potential customers that some might be satisfied with this being their main smartphone, which has prompted a handful of changes to improve the overall experience.

By far, the biggest upgrade is a move from 8GB to 12GB of RAM, something I’ll be calling a “reverse Pixel 11 Pro” situation. While other smartphone makers are doing whatever they can to reduce RAM — while increasing prices along the way — Clicks is adding additional memory to the device to better futureproof the phone. Its upgrade policy isn’t quite on par with Google or Samsung, but three promised OS upgrades and five years of security updates will, at the very least, pull your Communicator through to around 2032. Clicks has also moved its launch platform to Android 17 out of the box and bumped its battery capacity up to 4,350mAh. 

On the accessory side, Clicks and Dbrand are bringing the latter’s new MNML cases to the device, along with its Prism screen protector that includes a self-aligning tray — is there any other way? Clicks will also continue to offer its bumper Ring case for those looking for a more minimal approach to protection. Dbrand’s case and screen protector will run you $39 and $35, respectively, while the Ring bumper case is $49. Additional Charging Covers, allowing you to switch up your phone’s design, will also be available for $50 or $80, depending on material.

	

Finally, Clicks is launching both a protection plan and eSIM options for its users. Clicks Care is a $129 protection plan that delivers replacements or repairs for accidental damage over a two-year term with a $49 deductible; it’ll be available in the US and Canada. Clicks Mobile, meanwhile, is a new MVNO offering that brings voice and data to the Communicator via eSIM in the US and UK. Subscribers will receive two months of free service when activating their device at launch.

Clicks Communicator is set to ship in December, with reservation holders getting invites today to configure their final orders. September 30th — about two weeks away — is the last day to pre-order the device at its $499 launch price; starting October 1st, it moves to its base MSRP of $650. Anyone who scores the device as its cheaper starting price won’t be asked to pay more for its battery or RAM upgrades.

fullText:
Dominic Preston

 

is a news editor with over a decade’s experience in journalism. He previously worked at Android Police and Tech Advisor.

Vivo’s new X500 flagship phones have arrived in China, and as usual the company’s focus is firmly on photography. The X500 Pro Max — a new tier in its lineup — is the first phone to use new sensors and silicon from Sony and MediaTek that enable impressive dynamic range and slow-motion video recording.

The X500 Pro Max uses Sony’s new Lytia L910 image sensor, its first to use LOFIC, a sensor technology that enables expanded dynamic range. The 50-megapixel, 1/1.28-inch-type sensor delivers what Vivo calls “true 17 EV ultra-high dynamic range,” more than the 16.5 stops claimed by the Xiaomi 17 Ultra. The excellent 200-megapixel, 3.7x telephoto from the X300 Ultra returns here too, along with support for that phone’s 400mm teleconverter lens.

The X500 Pro and Pro Max are also the first phones run on MediaTek’s new Dimensity 9600 Pro, with the 9600M found in the base X500. The 2nm Pro chip brings with it the usual performance bumps, but also the ability to record 4K 240fps slow-motion video. 10bit Log recording and new cinematic video styles are included too.

Display sizes range from the compact 6.36-inch Pro to the 6.85-inch Pro Max, with the base X500 in-between. All three phones feature OLED displays, silicon-carbon batteries between 6,510mAh and 8,000mAh in size, and run on Vivo’s OriginOS 7 software. Today’s launch is China-only, but a global launch is coming, though we don’t yet know when.
